import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Compute Welch's t-test p-values and effect sizes for all features
    feature_stats = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col_idx]
        y = feats.y
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(x[y==1], x[y==0], equal_var=False)
        effect_size = np.mean(x[y==1]) - np.mean(x[y==0])
        feature_stats.append((abs(effect_size), p_val, fid))
    
    # Sort by effect size (largest first)
    feature_stats.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Take top features, but cap at MAX_DRIVERS
    top_features = [fid for _, _, fid in feature_stats[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # If no features show strong association, return empty design
    if not top_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Build regression components
    columns = top_features.copy()
    
    # Add interaction terms for top features (at most 4 interactions)
    products = []
    for i in range(min(2, len(top_features))):
        for j in range(i+1, min(3, len(top_features))):
            products.append((top_features[i], top_features[j]))
    
    # Compute weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(top_features):
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col_idx]
        y = feats.y
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(x[y==1], x[y==0], equal_var=False)
        # Use effect size as loading weight
        effect_size = np.mean(x[y==1]) - np.mean(x[y==0])
        loadings[fid] = effect_size
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(top_features),
        columns=tuple(columns),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
